zh-TW.long_thesis_markdown:
## 假日固定收益簡報

美國固定收益市場9月7日因勞動節休市，當天沒有美國公債價格發現；美國與伊朗衝突升級推高能源成本，也加重其他地區央行面臨的通膨壓力。布蘭特原油一度觸及每桶$98.06的6週高點，終場上漲1.1%至$97.31。WTI原油截至紐約午後早盤上漲1.3%至$92.65，但因假日未結算。

這場歷時6個月的衝突在週末爆發規模最大的一輪油輪與軍艦相互攻擊。伊朗國會議長Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf揚言，若美國進一步攻擊，伊朗將予以報復。荷莫茲海峽航運仍受到嚴重限制；Kpler統計，過去10天平均每天僅有10艘商品運輸船通行，為5月以來最低。高盛表示，若針對航運的攻擊加劇，原油可能升至$120。

伊朗與阿曼可能達成協議，為局勢帶來緩和契機，但尚不足以化解危機。德黑蘭表示，談判已進入最後階段，雙方將在荷莫茲海峽設立一條臨時安全航道。消息一度使油價收斂漲幅，但在沙烏地阿拉伯能源基礎設施遇襲的報導傳出後，油價再度走高。伊朗也表示將在海峽外劃設限制區，但其條件、執行方式及美國反應仍未明朗。OPEC+則維持10月產量政策不變。

能源衝擊強化了歐洲央行近期升息的理由，但也使後續政策路徑更為複雜。交易員已完全反映歐洲央行9月10日將存款利率調升25個基點至2.5%，並認為進一步緊縮的機率很高。不過，多數經濟學家預期歐洲央行會在9月升息後暫停，原因是目前尚無明確證據顯示能源成本上漲已廣泛擴散：服務通膨已下降、薪資成長放緩，勞動市場狀況也依然疲弱。

日本則帶來另一股全球政策壓力。日本首相高市早苗的經濟顧問Takuji Aida，將日本央行下次升息的預測時點由2027年1月提前至9月17日至18日會議。他認為，10月初召開臨時國會前的9月是短暫的政策窗口，並預期日本央行會在明年1月再次升息，之後約每6個月緊縮一次。市場已幾乎完全反映升息25個基點至1.25%。

## 全球利率、信用與主權債市發展

歐洲承受的通膨風險以天然氣最為嚴峻。自伊朗戰爭爆發以來，天然氣價格已上漲逾120%，庫存則處於歷來同期最低水準。各國政府與企業可能因夏季延後採購，等到冬季逼近時才與亞洲買家競購，投資人與官員正面對這項風險。部分市場人士認為，價格可能突破每兆瓦時€100，較當前水準高約40%。

影響不僅限於市場預期中的歐洲央行決策。過去一個月，法國、義大利與英國的長天期借款成本升幅均超過其他七大工業國發行人；投資人持有30年期德國公債所要求的補償，也升至2011年以來最高。財政擴張與政治不確定性正進一步放大能源衝擊：法國赤字超過GDP的5%，德國計畫在2027年新增逾€2,000億債務，義大利則在經歷一段相對穩定期後，將於明年舉行大選。

近期經濟數據給了歐洲央行相互矛盾的訊號。德國7月工業生產下滑1.1%，遜於市場預期的成長0.1%。汽車業因停工數週，產出大減9.2%，抵銷能源生產成長4.7%及營建業成長0.9%的效果。萊茵河水位偏低，可能在8月與9月進一步拖累生產；經濟學家也不預期較強的工廠訂單能在第4季前帶動產出回升。

Sentix投資人信心則明顯轉強。歐元區指數連續第5個月上升，9月由0.9升至5.1，不僅遠高於2.0的預測，也是2022年2月以來最高。現況指數由-8.0改善至-3.3，預期指數上升3.5點至13.8。德國指數則由-11.9升至-2.8，創2025年7月以來最佳表現。信心改善與疲弱的工業硬數據形成對比，歐洲央行須據此判斷，能源衝擊是否需要一次保險性升息以外的更多行動。

德國另類選擇黨在薩克森－安哈特邦選舉取得44%選票，創該黨邦級選舉最佳成績，距絕對多數僅差3席，政治風險也因而更直接進入德國長天期公債定價。總理Friedrich Merz表示，執政聯盟必須從選舉結果中汲取教訓，同時維持既定目標。另有兩場邦級選舉將於9月20日舉行，眼前焦點在於Merz面臨的壓力是否會拖延旨在更有效運用德國財政擴張的改革。

現有跡象已顯示，這項支出計畫帶來的新增投資低於市場最初預期。Ifo研究所估計，去年指定用於支出的債務中，有95%被拿來填補一般預算缺口。德國憲政架構使這項€5,000億方案難以逆轉，但執行成效欠佳、融資成本上升，加上另類選擇黨勢力增強，都提高改革遭稀釋或延後的風險。

英國也面臨借款成本與財政企圖相互衝突。財政大臣John Healey在首次重大演說中承諾，10月28日公布預算時將遵守財政規則；政府會保留應對不確定性的緩衝空間、控制借款，並減輕公共財政的長期壓力。能源衝擊帶動債務成本上升，已開始侵蝕這項緩衝。經濟學家估計，3月計算的£236億餘裕約有一半已經流失。

Healey在強調財政節制的同時，也提出規模較小的供給面措施，包括向英國商業銀行提供£1.5億、加強英格蘭北部城市區域與國家財富基金的合作，以及在2029年前將企業監管減少25%。依規則，公共金融機構可以舉債，只要所發放貸款被視為可抵銷的資產，但相關債務利息成本仍須計入。這項安排讓政府得以在不放棄債務目標的情況下支持投資，但融資成本愈高，其效用就愈有限。

房市已顯示這股壓力正向國內傳導。Lloyds公布，8月房價較一年前下跌0.4%，是2023年11月以來首次出現年減，也遜於預期的成長0.2%。房價較前月下跌0.2%，7月原先公布的漲幅也被修正為下跌。Nationwide的另一項指標顯示房價年增1.6%，反映不確定的是放緩速度，而非房市正在降溫的方向。Capital Economics估計，近期市場利率上升，可能使典型2年期固定房貸利率從7月的4.8%升至9月接近5%。

日本政策轉向持續影響匯率與政府債券需求。日圓在倫敦交易時段一度升值1.4%至每美元兌154.06日圓，為2月以來最高，並超越日本與美國協同干預後觸及的高點。交易員認為，走勢來自匯價突破155、美元停損賣盤、投資組合再平衡及假日期間流動性偏薄，而非單一新催化因素。

不過，日圓升值的根本仍是政策展望已明顯轉鷹。日本央行審議委員高田創未排除較大幅度或連續升息，總裁植田和男也表示，9月會議將依通膨風險展開討論；Aida調整預測則顯示，政府內部對政策正常化的阻力正在減弱。財務大臣片山皋月重申，相關決定仍由日本央行作出。

日本8月持有的外國證券創紀錄減少$878億，規模接近近期匯市干預，顯示當局可能出售包括短天期美國公債在內的海外資產，協助支應干預行動。與此同時，日本央行持續縮減國內債券購買，使民間買家必須承接更多供給。日本央行7月持有的JGB較一年前減少¥47.8兆，是1997年開始統計以來最大降幅。

中國選擇支援資產負債表，而非收緊政策。5家國有保險公司與3家銀行宣布，計畫透過財政部及其他股東注資，籌集最多3,600億元人民幣。財政部擬發行3,000億元人民幣特別國債為計畫提供資金，這也是中國首次使用該工具為保險公司及銀行補充資本。

5家保險公司預計將獲得700億元人民幣，其中中國人壽取得350億元，中國太平取得70億元。中國人保另計畫向財政部私募最多150億元人民幣。GMF Research估計，投入4家商業保險公司的600億元人民幣，可支撐約1,000億元人民幣的額外股票曝險。這些交易將增強吸收損失的能力與放款潛力，但也會增加主權債供給並稀釋股權；保險與銀行類股指數分別下跌2.5%與1.5%。

與此同時，中國的外部緩衝有所改善。8月外匯存底由$3.419兆增至$3.438兆，高於市場共識的$3.425兆。美元兌一籃子主要貨幣當月下跌0.4%，人民幣則升值0.49%。

特殊方案為印度金融體系帶來逾$1,360億資金，使印度央行面對相反的流動性問題。9月6日，銀行體系剩餘流動性創下11.6兆盧比的紀錄，接近存款的4%。印度央行隔日透過一項30天期操作與隔夜標售，吸收逾6兆盧比；銀行投入2.59兆盧比參與30天期操作，另於隔夜標售申報3.53兆盧比。

30天期操作的承作量遠低於印度央行7兆盧比的目標。5名交易員將此歸因於技術問題，但一名知情人士表示，所有投標均順利透過e-Kuber系統，並未發生故障。印度央行合計收回的流動性超過8.5兆盧比；IDFC First Bank認為，下一步可能採用市場穩定計畫債券或外匯先賣後買交換。兩者都可能使貨幣市場維持較緊狀態，但發債也會增加用於沖銷流動性的債券供給。

匯市干預進一步擴大流動性回收。6名銀行業人士估計，截至9月4日的一週，印度央行至少賣出$80億，最高估計達$150億，各項估計的中間值至少是前一週交易量的3倍。這些操作協助盧比在9月3日升至每美元兌94.2850盧比，創逾2個月新高。支撐干預的是截至8月21日創紀錄的$7,408億官方外匯存底，以及折價或免費避險方案帶來的異常龐大資金流入。出售美元在支撐盧比的同時，也會從市場抽走盧比，使匯率防衛直接連結到前端融資狀況。

新興市場需求仍具選擇性，並非全面轉向防禦。外國投資人在8月投入$39億買進馬來西亞政府債與公司債，是該國央行2016年開始統計以來最大單月流入。投資人認為資料中心投資將帶動出口與外國直接投資，馬來西亞令吉當月因而升值逾1%。本幣新興市場債券今年以來報酬率為3.6%，與主要已開發國家主權債市的虧損形成對比，支撐因素包括原本偏緊的利率水準，以及開發中經濟體平均通膨率僅3.8%。

個別發行人的信用發展則更為分歧。澳洲已無力償債的Bathla Group獲得5家貸款機構提供過渡資金，可維持部分業務運作兩週，管理人Teneo則繼續尋求更全面的融資方案。一名熟悉談判的人士估計，融資金額接近A$400萬，但Teneo並未證實。與參與融資的貸款機構相關之建案仍持續施工，其他地點則已停工，約213名員工停止工作。

短暫的融資期限凸顯資產與負債之間的巨大落差。Bathla欠款A$34億，包括欠有擔保貸款機構A$31億及無擔保債權人A$1.3億。澳洲證券監管機關正在調查借款去向，以及散戶投資人是否透過私募信貸基金承受曝險。這項緊急融資只能保護特定建案，無法支應集團旗下所有工程完工，也不能決定持有不同擔保品的貸款機構最終可收回多少資金。

Cerba Healthcare的重整也延伸至次級貸款交易。這家法國檢驗集團正就€50億債務推進法院監督下的調解程序，一家或多家貸款機構則為其€4.5億循環信貸額度中的約€2,800萬部位徵求報價。這類信貸額度的交易頻率低於債券；重整日益逼近之際，若部位折價出售給專業基金，可能改變談判影響力。Cerba一筆2028年到期、規模€7.2億的有擔保債券，報價約為每1歐元面額70歐分，高於季度業績改善及調解消息公布前的68.6歐分。

對融資管道較暢通的借款人而言，初級市場仍然開放。Uber開始為首次發行的5期歐元債券與投資人溝通，年期涵蓋3年、6年、8年、12年與20年；今年以來美國企業赴歐洲發債的規模已接近創紀錄的€1,250億。MTN離開歐洲債券市場10年後，在倫敦舉行非交易型路演。該公司最後一筆$5億國際債券將於10月到期，但公司表示有足夠資源償還；更大的融資問題是擬以$22億收購IHS Towers剩餘股份，管理層預期部分收購款將以舉債支應。

印度國營企業REC完成該國首筆代幣化公司債，透過2028年5月到期、票息7.30%的債券籌得50億盧比。約20名投資人參與，包括銀行、共同基金與企業，交割則使用印度央行數位貨幣；據報HDFC Bank與ICICI Bank也在買家之列。這項試辦計畫把代幣化證券與央行貨幣相連，可能縮短配售與交割時間。Larsen & Toubro也為最多50億盧比、3年期的代幣化債券徵求報價。

烏克蘭的主權融資風險仍然嚴峻。針對價值低於€150的進口包裹課徵加值稅之法案初審未獲通過後，國會計畫再度嘗試表決。IMF將這項措施視為關鍵融資條件，其代表團也告知議員，不應期待獲得豁免。烏克蘭2026年預算赤字將超過$320億，若無法通過該措施，經濟與社會支出獲得官方援助的時程恐受威脅。

紐約聯準銀行的研究，為市場對官方外匯存底配置美元資產需求的疑慮提供較長期的補充視角。美元占官方外匯存底的比重，已由10年前的64%降至去年的56%；但研究發現，自2015年以來的兩段期間中，提高與降低美元配置的國家數量大致相同。2015年至2019年的主動再配置主要由中國與俄羅斯造成；截至2023年的降幅，則多由這兩國加上墨西哥與摩洛哥所推動。因此，整體占比變化主要反映大型外匯存底管理者的集中決策，而非各國普遍撤出美元。

## 下一交易日觀察重點

美國市場重新開市後，將立即面對通膨風險與美國公債供給的雙重考驗。9月8日將公布NFIB企業樂觀指數、ADP每週就業估計、8月中古車價格及消費者通膨預期。NFIB指數預計由99.8降至99.3，通膨預期則維持在3.6%。3個月與6個月期國庫券標售後，當天稍晚還有6週期國庫券與3年期公債標售。由於勞動節當天沒有現券交易，這些標售將是週末能源局勢升級後，市場對美國政府債券需求的首次直接檢驗。

供給時程在9月9日延續，當天將標售17週期國庫券與10年期公債。截至9月4日當週的房貸申請與利率，可顯示借款環境如何傳導至房市；6月雇主薪酬數據則會在主要通膨數據公布前，提供一項勞動成本指標。

8月生產者物價與每週初領失業救濟金人數將於9月10日公布。整體PPI預計月增0.4%，前月為零成長；核心PPI則預計由前月的0.2%增幅加快至0.3%。初領失業救濟金人數預計約20.5萬，續領人數則為179萬。歐洲央行同日公布決策；由於升息至2.5%已完全反映在市場價格中，相較於預期中的本次升息，其政策指引會否顯示能源壓力足以支持12月再次升息，可能更為重要。

美國8月消費者物價與實質薪資將於9月11日公布，構成9月15日至16日聯準會會議前最後一批主要證據。聯準會主席Kevin Warsh強調，基礎通膨改善不足；紐約聯準銀行總裁John Williams認為關稅影響正在消退；理事Christopher Waller則更重視近期、較短期的物價趨勢。這些數據將決定上述分歧最終導向利率不變或進一步升息。

日本央行9月17日至18日的決策，如今也是市場檢驗普遍預期升息25個基點後政策路徑的關鍵。若9月升息，將印證Aida提前升息的預測，也會驗證日圓近期的部分重新定價。日本央行對明年1月再次升息的指引、JGB資產負債表縮減速度，以及政府對較高利率的容忍度，將決定市場把本次調整視為單次行動，還是更快速正常化循環的起點。

能源實體供給情勢仍是足以改變上述所有判斷的跨市場條件。若阿曼與伊朗能建立可行的航運走廊，部分商業航運可望恢復，油價與歐洲天然氣價格壓力也可能減輕。反之，若攻擊持續、伊朗限制區確實執行，或波斯灣基礎設施進一步受損，央行升息以對抗通膨的理由將更強，即使融資成本與家庭能源支出上升會削弱經濟成長。

overall_summary.headline: 勞動節休市之際，美國債市面臨更嚴峻的油價通膨考驗
overall_summary.session_narrative:
美國固定收益市場9月7日因勞動節休市，當天沒有美國公債價格發現。這場歷時6個月的美國與伊朗衝突爆發規模最大的一輪油輪與軍艦相互攻擊，使荷莫茲海峽過去10天平均每天僅有10艘商品運輸船通行。布蘭特原油觸及$98.06後，終場上漲1.1%至$97.31。阿曼與伊朗擬議的安全航道一度抑制油價漲勢，但沙烏地阿拉伯能源基礎設施再度遇襲，加上伊朗限制區的條件仍未確定，實體供給風險並未解除。

這項衝擊強化歐洲央行9月10日升息25個基點至2.5%的近期理由，市場也已完全反映這項調整；然而，服務通膨下降、薪資成長放緩及勞動市場疲弱，使後續升息仍具不確定性。在日本，Takuji Aida將日本央行下次升息的預測提前至9月17日至18日，市場已幾乎完全反映升息25個基點至1.25%。較緊的政策展望支撐日圓升至每美元兌154.06日圓，日本央行縮減購債則讓民間買家承接更多JGB供給。

其他市場方面，中國計畫為5家保險公司與3家銀行提供最多3,600億元人民幣的資本支持，部分資金將透過發行3,000億元人民幣特別國債籌措。印度銀行體系則出現創紀錄的11.6兆盧比剩餘流動性；印度央行收回逾8.5兆盧比，賣出美元也進一步抽走市場資金。美國市場重開後將面對公債標售與通膨數據，而荷莫茲海峽航運走向仍是最迫切的跨市場考驗。
overall_summary.summary: 美伊衝突升級，限制荷莫茲海峽航運並將布蘭特原油推高至$97.31，加劇全球通膨風險；市場預期歐洲央行與日本央行收緊政策，也為美國下一交易日定下政策背景。

section_summaries.summary: 美國固定收益市場休市之際，針對油輪、軍艦與沙烏地阿拉伯能源基礎設施的攻擊把布蘭特原油推升至$97.31，荷莫茲海峽航運仍受到嚴重限制。阿曼與伊朗擬議的安全航道尚未解決危機。能源衝擊強化了市場已完全反映的歐洲央行9月10日升息25個基點，但不足以確立更長的升息循環；日本則帶來另一股緊縮壓力，市場已幾乎完全反映日本央行9月17日至18日升息至1.25%。

section_summaries.market_read: 印度央行賣出美元，在支撐盧比的同時抽走國內流動性，使匯率防衛直接連結到前端融資狀況。

section_summaries.summary: 歐洲天然氣衝擊與德國工業生產疲弱、Sentix信心轉強，以及法國、義大利、德國和英國日益加重的財政與長天期借款成本壓力同時出現。日本政策展望轉鷹，帶動日圓升值，也使民間買家承接更多JGB供給。中國在規劃3,600億元人民幣銀行與保險業資本方案的同時，將發行3,000億元人民幣主權債；印度央行則回收創紀錄的剩餘流動性。信用需求仍具選擇性：馬來西亞債市吸引$39億資金流入，Bathla僅取得兩週融資，Cerba債務逐步進入調解程序，融資管道較暢通的發行人則繼續籌資。
美國市場重新開市後，9月8日將迎來勞動、企業信心、中古車價格與通膨預期數據，以及假日後首批美國公債標售。供給時程延續至9月9日的10年期公債標售；9月10日將公布PPI與初領失業救濟金人數，歐洲央行也在同日決策；9月11日公布CPI，隨後是9月15日至16日聯準會會議。日本央行將於9月17日至18日決策，而荷莫茲海峽通行狀況的任何變化，都可能重塑這一連串考驗所處的通膨與成長背景。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Holiday Fixed-Income Brief

U.S. fixed-income markets were closed for Labor Day on Sept. 7, leaving no same-day Treasury price discovery as an escalating U.S.-Iran conflict lifted energy costs and added to the inflation pressure facing central banks elsewhere. Brent settled at $97.31 a barrel, up 1.1%, after reaching a six-week high of $98.06. WTI rose 1.3% to $92.65 by early afternoon in New York but did not settle because of the holiday.

The weekend brought the largest exchange of tanker and warship attacks in the six-month conflict. Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf threatened retaliation for further U.S. attacks, while shipping through the Strait of Hormuz remained severely constrained: Kpler counted an average of 10 commodity-vessel transits a day over the previous 10 days, the lowest since May. Goldman Sachs said crude could reach $120 if attacks on shipping intensified.

A possible Iranian agreement with Oman offered a countervailing development but not yet a resolution. Tehran said negotiations were in their final stages and would establish a temporary safe route through Hormuz. Oil briefly pared gains on the news before rising again after reports of strikes on Saudi energy infrastructure. Iran also said it would announce a restricted zone outside the strait, leaving the terms, enforcement and U.S. response unresolved. OPEC+ kept its October production policy unchanged.

The energy shock sharpened the immediate case for a widely expected European Central Bank increase while complicating the path beyond it. Traders fully priced a 25-basis-point rise in the deposit rate to 2.5% on Sept. 10 and assigned a high probability to further tightening. Economists generally expected the ECB to stop after September, however, because there was not yet clear evidence that higher energy costs were spreading broadly: services inflation had fallen, wage growth was slowing and labor conditions remained soft.

Japan supplied a second source of global policy pressure. Takuji Aida, an economic adviser to Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, brought his forecast for the next Bank of Japan increase forward from January 2027 to the Sept. 17-18 meeting. He described September as a narrow opportunity before an extraordinary parliamentary session in early October and expected another increase by January, followed by a roughly six-month tightening cadence. Markets had nearly fully priced a 25-basis-point move to 1.25%.

## Global Rates, Credit, And Sovereign Developments

Europe’s inflation exposure was most acute in natural gas. Prices had risen more than 120% since the Iran war began, while storage stood at a record seasonal low. Investors and officials were confronting the possibility that governments and companies delayed purchases over the summer only to compete with Asian buyers as winter approached. Some market participants saw prices potentially exceeding €100 per megawatt-hour, about 40% above prevailing levels.

The consequences extended beyond the expected ECB decision. Longer-dated French, Italian and UK borrowing costs had risen more than those of other Group of Seven issuers over the preceding month, while investors demanded the greatest compensation since 2011 to hold 30-year German debt. Fiscal expansion and political uncertainty were reinforcing the energy effect: France’s deficit exceeded 5% of GDP, Germany planned more than €200 billion of new debt for 2027, and Italy faced an election next year after a period of relative stability.

Current economic releases gave the ECB conflicting signals. German industrial production fell 1.1% in July instead of rising 0.1% as expected. Automotive output dropped 9.2% during a multi-week shutdown, overwhelming gains of 4.7% in energy production and 0.9% in construction. Low Rhine water levels threatened a further restraint in August and September, and economists did not expect stronger factory orders to lift production before the fourth quarter.

Sentix investor confidence was considerably firmer. The euro-area index rose for a fifth month, to 5.1 in September from 0.9, well above the 2.0 forecast and its highest level since February 2022. Current conditions improved to -3.3 from -8.0, while expectations increased 3.5 points to 13.8. Germany’s reading climbed to -2.8 from -11.9, its best since July 2025. The contrast leaves the ECB with improving sentiment but weak hard industrial data as it judges whether the energy shock requires more than an insurance increase.

Political risk also moved closer to the center of German duration pricing after the Alternative for Germany won 44% in Saxony-Anhalt, its best result in a state election and three seats short of an absolute majority. Chancellor Friedrich Merz said his coalition needed to learn from the result while maintaining its goals. Two more state votes are due Sept. 20, and the immediate question is whether pressure on Merz delays reforms intended to make better use of Germany’s fiscal expansion.

There was already evidence that the spending program had delivered less incremental investment than markets initially anticipated. The Ifo institute estimated that 95% of debt earmarked for spending last year was used to fill holes in the regular budget. Germany’s constitutional framework makes the €500 billion package difficult to reverse, but the combination of weak execution, rising financing costs and a stronger AfD increases the risk of diluted or delayed reforms.

The UK faced a similar collision between borrowing costs and fiscal ambition. Chancellor John Healey used his first major speech to pledge adherence to the fiscal rules at the Oct. 28 budget, saying the government would maintain a buffer against uncertainty, control borrowing and reduce long-term pressure on the public finances. Higher debt costs linked to the energy shock were already eroding that buffer, with economists estimating that roughly half of the £23.6 billion margin calculated in March had been lost.

Healey paired fiscal restraint with smaller supply-side measures, including £150 million for the British Business Bank, closer cooperation between northern city regions and the National Wealth Fund, and a target to reduce business regulation by 25% by 2029. The rules permit borrowing by public financial institutions when the resulting loans are treated as offsetting assets, although the associated debt-service cost still counts. That structure gives the government a route to support investment without abandoning its debt target, but it becomes less useful as financing costs rise.

Housing showed the domestic transmission already under way. Lloyds reported that prices fell 0.4% from a year earlier in August, the first annual decline since November 2023 and weaker than the expected 0.2% increase. Prices dropped 0.2% on the month, and July’s previously reported gain was revised into a decline. Nationwide’s separate measure showed 1.6% annual growth, underlining the uncertainty around the pace rather than the direction of the slowdown. Capital Economics estimated that recent market-rate increases could lift a typical two-year fixed mortgage rate toward 5% in September from 4.8% in July.

In Japan, the policy shift continued to reach both the currency and government-debt demand. The yen strengthened as much as 1.4% to 154.06 per dollar in London, its highest since February and beyond the peak reached after coordinated intervention by Japan and the United States. Traders cited a break through 155, stop-loss selling of dollars, portfolio rebalancing and thin holiday liquidity rather than a single new catalyst.

The move was nevertheless rooted in a materially tighter policy outlook. BOJ board member Hajime Takata had left open larger or consecutive increases, Governor Kazuo Ueda had said September would include a debate based on inflation risks, and Aida’s revised call suggested resistance to normalization inside the government was weakening. Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama reiterated that the decision remained the BOJ’s.

Japan’s foreign-securities holdings fell by a record $87.8 billion during August, close to the scale of its recent currency intervention, suggesting that authorities sold foreign assets, including short-dated Treasuries, to help finance the operation. Meanwhile, the BOJ’s retreat from domestic bond purchases continued to leave private buyers with more supply to absorb. Its JGB holdings were ¥47.8 trillion lower in July than a year earlier, the largest decline in data extending back to 1997.

China chose balance-sheet support rather than tighter policy. Five state-owned insurers and three banks announced plans to raise as much as 360 billion yuan through capital injections from the Finance Ministry and other shareholders. The ministry planned 300 billion yuan of special sovereign bonds to fund the program, marking the first use of the instrument to recapitalize insurers as well as banks.

The five insurers were set to receive 70 billion yuan, including 35 billion yuan for China Life and 7 billion yuan for China Taiping. PICC separately planned a private placement of as much as 15 billion yuan to the Finance Ministry. GMF Research estimated that 60 billion yuan directed to four commercial insurers could support roughly 100 billion yuan of additional equity exposure. The transaction strengthens loss-absorbing capacity and lending potential, but it also introduces sovereign supply and dilution: insurance and banking equity indexes fell 2.5% and 1.5%, respectively.

China’s external buffer improved at the same time. Foreign-exchange reserves increased to $3.438 trillion in August from $3.419 trillion, exceeding the $3.425 trillion consensus. The yuan appreciated 0.49% during the month as the dollar weakened 0.4% against a basket of major currencies.

India’s central bank confronted the opposite liquidity problem after special schemes brought more than $136 billion into the financial system. The banking surplus reached a record 11.6 trillion rupees on Sept. 6, close to 4% of deposits. The Reserve Bank of India absorbed more than 6 trillion rupees the next day through a 30-day operation and an overnight auction; banks placed 2.59 trillion rupees for 30 days and offered another 3.53 trillion overnight.

The 30-day take-up fell well short of the RBI’s 7 trillion-rupee target. Five traders blamed technical problems, while a person familiar with the operation said all bids passed through the e-Kuber system without glitches. Total RBI withdrawals exceeded 8.5 trillion rupees, and IDFC First Bank identified Market Stabilisation Scheme bonds and sell-buy currency swaps as possible next steps. Either could keep money-market conditions tighter, although bond issuance would also add sterilization supply.

Currency intervention amplified that drain. Six bankers estimated that the RBI sold at least $8 billion during the week through Sept. 4, with estimates ranging as high as $15 billion and the midpoint assessments running at least three times the previous week’s volume. The operations helped the rupee reach a more-than-two-month high of 94.2850 per dollar on Sept. 3. They were backed by record official reserves of $740.8 billion as of Aug. 21 and by the extraordinary inflows from discounted or free hedging programs. Dollar sales support the currency while removing rupees, linking exchange-rate defense directly to front-end funding conditions.

Emerging-market demand remained selective rather than uniformly defensive. Foreign investors placed $3.9 billion into Malaysian government and corporate bonds during August, the largest monthly inflow in central-bank data beginning in 2016. The ringgit gained more than 1% over the month as investors associated data-center investment with stronger exports and foreign direct investment. Across local-currency emerging-market bonds, year-to-date returns of 3.6% contrasted with losses in major developed sovereign markets, supported by restrictive starting rates and average developing-economy inflation of 3.8%.

Issuer-level credit developments were more disparate. Australia’s insolvent Bathla Group obtained stopgap funding from five lenders to keep limited operations running for two weeks while administrator Teneo pursued a broader package. A person familiar with the negotiations put the financing near A$4 million, although Teneo did not confirm the amount. Work continued on projects linked to participating lenders, while construction elsewhere was suspended and about 213 employees stopped work.

The short runway underscores the scale of the mismatch. Bathla owes A$3.4 billion, including A$3.1 billion to secured lenders and A$130 million to unsecured creditors. Australia’s securities regulator is investigating where the borrowed money went and whether retail investors were exposed through private-credit funds. The emergency facility protects selected projects; it does not finance completion across the group or determine recoveries among lenders with different collateral.

Cerba Healthcare’s restructuring also moved into secondary loan trading. One or more lenders sought bids for about €28 million of its €450 million revolving facility as the French laboratory group advanced toward court-supervised conciliation over €5 billion of debt. Such facilities trade less frequently than bonds, and sales to specialist funds at discounts can shift negotiating influence as a restructuring approaches. Cerba’s €720 million secured bond due in 2028 was marked near 70 cents on the euro, up from 68.6 before improving quarterly results and the conciliation announcement.

Primary markets remained available for borrowers with clearer access. Uber began investor calls for a debut five-part euro transaction spanning three, six, eight, 12 and 20 years, joining record reverse-yankee issuance of almost €125 billion so far this year. MTN held a non-deal roadshow in London after a decade away from the Eurobond market. Its final $500 million international note matures in October, but the company said it had resources to repay it; the larger financing question is its proposed $2.2 billion purchase of the remaining shares in IHS Towers, which management expects to fund partly with debt.

India’s state-run REC completed the country’s first tokenized corporate bond, raising 5 billion rupees through notes due in May 2028 with a 7.30% coupon. Roughly 20 investors participated, including banks, mutual funds and companies, and settlement used the RBI’s digital currency. HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank were among the reported buyers. The pilot linked tokenized securities to central-bank money, potentially shortening allotment and settlement, while Larsen & Toubro sought bids for as much as 5 billion rupees of three-year tokenized notes.

Sovereign financing risk remained acute in Ukraine. Parliament planned another attempt to pass value-added tax on imported parcels worth less than €150 after the bill failed its first reading. The IMF regards the measure as a critical funding condition, and its mission told lawmakers not to expect an exception. With Ukraine facing a 2026 budget deficit exceeding $32 billion, failure to enact the measure would threaten the timing of official support for the economy and social spending.

Research from the Federal Reserve Bank of New York supplied a longer-horizon qualification to concerns about reserve demand for dollar assets. The dollar’s share of official reserves declined to 56% last year from 64% a decade earlier, but the study found roughly equal numbers of countries increasing and reducing their allocations in two periods since 2015. China and Russia accounted for most active reallocation in 2015-2019; those two countries plus Mexico and Morocco drove much of the decline through 2023. The aggregate change therefore reflected concentrated decisions by large managers more than a uniform retreat from the currency.

## Next Open-Session Watch

U.S. trading reopens to an immediate combination of inflation risk and Treasury supply. Sept. 8 brings the NFIB business-optimism index, weekly ADP employment estimate, August used-car prices and consumer inflation expectations. The NFIB index is expected at 99.3 after 99.8, while the inflation-expectations forecast remains 3.6%. Three- and six-month bill auctions are followed later by six-week bills and the 3-year note sale. With no Labor Day cash session, those auctions will provide the first direct test of U.S. government-debt demand after the weekend’s energy escalation.

The supply sequence continues with 17-week bills and the 10-year note on Sept. 9. Mortgage applications and rates for the week through Sept. 4 will show how borrowing conditions are reaching housing, while June employer-compensation data add a labor-cost reading before the main inflation releases.

August producer prices and weekly jobless claims arrive Sept. 10. Headline PPI is expected to rise 0.4% after no monthly change, and core PPI is expected to increase 0.3% after 0.2%. Initial claims are expected near 205,000 and continuing claims at 1.79 million. The ECB decides the same day; because a rise to 2.5% is fully priced, guidance on whether energy pressure justifies another move by December is likely to matter more than the anticipated increase itself.

August U.S. consumer prices and real earnings follow Sept. 11, completing the principal evidence available before the Sept. 15-16 Federal Reserve meeting. Chair Kevin Warsh has emphasized insufficient improvement in underlying inflation, while New York Fed President John Williams sees tariff effects fading and Governor Christopher Waller has placed more weight on recent, shorter-run price trends. The data will determine whether those differences produce a hold or a further increase.

Japan’s Sept. 17-18 decision is now a test of the path beyond a widely expected 25-basis-point move. A September increase would validate Aida’s accelerated forecast and part of the yen’s recent repricing. Guidance on another move by January, the pace of JGB balance-sheet runoff and the government’s tolerance for higher rates will decide whether the change is treated as a single adjustment or a faster normalization cycle.

The physical energy situation remains the cross-market condition capable of changing all of those readings. A workable Oman-Iran shipping corridor could restore some commercial traffic and reduce the pressure on oil and European gas. Continued attacks, an enforceable Iranian restricted zone or further damage to Gulf infrastructure would instead strengthen the inflation case for central banks even as higher financing and household energy costs weaken growth.

section_summaries.summary: With U.S. fixed-income markets closed, attacks on tankers, warships and Saudi energy infrastructure pushed Brent to $97.31 and left Hormuz traffic severely constrained. A possible Oman-Iran safe route remained unresolved. The energy shock reinforced a fully priced 25-basis-point ECB increase on Sept. 10 but not the case for a longer cycle, while Japan added a separate tightening impulse as markets nearly fully priced a Sept. 17-18 BOJ move to 1.25%.

section_summaries.market_read: RBI dollar sales supported the rupee while removing domestic liquidity, directly linking FX defense to front-end funding conditions.
section_summaries.section_title: Global Rates, Credit, And Sovereign Developments
section_summaries.summary: Europe's gas shock collided with weak German production, stronger Sentix confidence and worsening fiscal-duration pressure in France, Italy, Germany and the UK. Japan's tighter policy outlook strengthened the yen and shifted more JGB supply to private buyers. China paired 360 billion yuan of bank-and-insurer capital plans with 300 billion yuan of sovereign issuance, while the RBI drained a record liquidity surplus. Credit stayed selective: Malaysia drew $3.9 billion of bond inflows, Bathla won only two weeks of funding, Cerba debt moved toward conciliation, and accessible issuers still pursued funding.

U.S. trading resumes with Sept. 8 labor, business, vehicle-price and inflation-expectations data alongside the first Treasury auctions after the holiday. The supply calendar extends to the Sept. 9 10-year sale, followed by PPI, jobless claims and the ECB on Sept. 10, then CPI on Sept. 11 ahead of the Sept. 15-16 Fed meeting. Japan decides on Sept. 17-18, while any change in Hormuz access could reshape the inflation and growth backdrop across these tests.

methodology_note: SIFMA recommends a full U.S. fixed-income market close for Labor Day. No prior-session market levels are presented as current-day moves.

overall_summary.headline: Labor Day closure leaves U.S. bonds facing a sharper oil-driven inflation test
overall_summary.session_narrative:
U.S. fixed-income markets were closed for Labor Day on Sept. 7, so there was no same-day Treasury price discovery. The largest tanker and warship exchange of the six-month U.S.-Iran conflict constrained Hormuz traffic to an average of 10 commodity-vessel transits a day over the prior 10 days. Brent settled 1.1% higher at $97.31 after touching $98.06. A proposed Oman-Iran safe route briefly tempered the move, but further strikes on Saudi energy infrastructure and unresolved terms for an Iranian restricted zone kept the physical supply risk open.

The shock strengthened the immediate case for a fully priced 25-basis-point ECB increase to 2.5% on Sept. 10, although softer services inflation, wages and labor conditions left further tightening uncertain. In Japan, Takuji Aida brought his forecast for the next BOJ increase forward to Sept. 17-18, with markets nearly fully pricing a 25-basis-point move to 1.25%. The tighter outlook underpinned the yen's rise to 154.06 per dollar, while BOJ runoff left private buyers absorbing more JGB supply.

Elsewhere, China planned up to 360 billion yuan of capital support for five insurers and three banks, funded in part by 300 billion yuan of special sovereign bonds. India faced a record 11.6 trillion-rupee banking surplus, and the RBI withdrew more than 8.5 trillion rupees as dollar sales also drained liquidity. U.S. trading reopens to Treasury auctions and inflation data, while the path of Hormuz shipping remains the nearest cross-market test.
overall_summary.summary: Escalating U.S.-Iran attacks constrained Hormuz traffic and lifted Brent to $97.31, deepening global inflation risk while expected ECB and BOJ tightening set the policy backdrop for the next U.S. session.

watch_events.market_implication: Relief would ease oil and gas pressure; disruption would reinforce inflation risk while weakening growth.
watch_events.market_trigger: Commercial transits recover under a workable corridor, or new attacks damage shipping or energy infrastructure.
watch_events.title: Hormuz shipping and Gulf infrastructure
watch_events.watch_line: Track whether an Oman-Iran corridor restores traffic or attacks and restrictions further impair Gulf flows.

watch_events.market_implication: Either would raise pressure on U.S. yields; softer inflation and firm auctions would reduce it.
watch_events.market_trigger: Weak auction demand or inflation above the 0.4% headline and 0.3% core PPI forecasts.
watch_events.title: U.S. inflation data and Treasury supply
watch_events.watch_line: Auctions, PPI and CPI provide the first demand and inflation tests before the Sept. 15-16 Fed meeting.

watch_events.market_implication: Hawkish guidance would extend pressure on European and Japanese borrowing costs and support the yen.
watch_events.market_trigger: ECB signals another move by December, or BOJ guides toward another increase by January and faster runoff.
watch_events.title: ECB and BOJ policy paths
watch_events.watch_line: ECB and BOJ guidance will show whether expected moves begin longer tightening sequences.
